dedupe_keys.name: injuries to pedestrians and bicyclists an analysis based on hospital emergency department data fhwa rd 99 078

description: This 1999 Federal Highway Administration report (FHWA-RD-99-078) analyses injuries to pedestrians and bicyclists from data collected prospectively at eight hospital emergency departments over about a year. Coverage: three states, California, New York and North Carolina, with 2,509 people treated for injuries while bicycling or walking. Contents: tables of injury events by location (roadway, non-roadway) and type (with or without a motor vehicle), crash circumstances, injury severity, alcohol involvement and comparisons with statewide hospital discharge and motor vehicle crash files; 70% of bicycle injury events and 64% of pedestrian events involved no motor vehicle, and 31% of bicyclists and 53% of pedestrians were hurt off the roadway, for example on sidewalks, parking lots or trails. Format and access: web chapters and a PDF on the FHWA site, with the survey form in an appendix. Licence and cost: free US government work. Caveats: an archived late-1990s sample from eight hospitals, so rates are not national; microdata are not published. It shows how much injury police crash files miss and can calibrate injury burdens for walking and cycling in hazard exposure studies. It relates to the GB STATS19 road safety data in the catalogue.
